_about: Sulfur dioxide (1) + iso-octane (2): total pressure against liquid composition at 20 degC from Nitta, Kido, Katayama (1976).

source.citation: T. Nitta, O. Kido, T. Katayama, Vapor-liquid equilibria for binary systems of sulfur dioxide and some organic solvents, J. Chem. Eng. Japan 9 (1976) 317-318
source.access: Open access to read on J-STAGE (marked Free access); copyright The Society of Chemical Engineers, Japan
source.tables: Table 1, iso-octane (A) block, p 317 (PDF p 1); x_B is the SO2 mole fraction; pressure 0.5 mmHg below 1000 mmHg, 3 mmHg above 1100 mmHg; liquid composition by iodometry
source.transcription: Read from the scanned page image at 200-400 dpi; compared value by value with an independent transcription in another assistant's literature package (they agree except where noted). The person checking should compare each row with the page.

excluded.reason: pure iso-octane: a vapour pressure taken from the authors' reference 1, not measured here

the pressure is almost constant (2378-2400 mmHg) from x = 0.64 to 0.85: a sign of two liquid phases (the authors report a large positive deviation from Raoult's law). A cubic equation of state with one k_ij is not used for liquid-liquid equilibrium here, so these rows are left out of the fit
